enabling_tech: Public-key cryptography; Young & Yung cryptovirology concept
scaled_definition: CryptoLocker reached 234,000+ infected computers by Apr 2014; a self-sustaining ransomware economy from ~2015
why_slow_or_fast: SLOW. The idea was published in 1996 but criminal use needed two missing pieces: reliable asymmetric crypto on the victim (early Gpcode keys were short enough to crack) and an anonymous payment rail (Bitcoin). Both matured ~2009-2013.
source_title: Cryptovirology: Extortion-Based Security Threats and Countermeasures
notes: AIDS Trojan (Dec 1989, 20,000 disks, $189 ransom, ~1,000 installs) predates the concept but used trivial symmetric filename-encryption, so it is not public-key cryptoviral extortion. First RSA criminal use = Gpcode.ac, Jan 2006 (Securelist). Availability=concept-publication year; lag_* measured from availability.

scaled_definition: Bitcoin the dominant ransom rail; FinCEN BSA data 2022-24 show Bitcoin = 97% of reported ransomware payment transactions (Monero 2%)
why_slow_or_fast: MEDIUM. Bitcoin existed from 2009; CryptoLocker (Sep 2013) was the first large-scale ransomware to demand it (alongside MoneyPak). All major families adopted it within ~3 years. Public ledger is a drawback criminals accept for pseudonymity.
source_title: Ransomware Trends in Bank Secrecy Act Data Between 2022 and 2024
notes: Satoshi v0.1 announced 2009-01-08 (metzdowd). CryptoLocker first-use and 234k/$27m-first-two-months from DOJ 2014-06-02. First-use->dominant ~3 years.

scaled_definition: A resilient multi-market ecosystem: Soska & Christin measured $300k-$500k/day (up to $650k/day 30-day avg), ~$150-180m/yr, 9,386 sellers across the ecosystem; survived Silk Road and Operation Onymous takedowns
why_slow_or_fast: SLOW from availability, FAST once seeded. Tor deployed 2002, free licence/EFF funding 2004; Silk Road did not launch until Feb 2011. But once Silk Road proved the model, the ecosystem reached scale and became takedown-resilient within ~3 years.
source_title: Measuring the Longitudinal Evolution of the Online Anonymous Marketplace Ecosystem
notes: Tor history dates from torproject.org/about/history (deployed Oct 2002; EFF funding 2004; nonprofit 2006). Silk Road Feb 2011 launch, ~1,400 sellers at Oct 2013 shutdown, >$200m / 100,000+ users (DOJ 2015-05-29). first-use->scaled ~3 years.

enabling_tech: Affiliate/platform business model + commodity ransomware builders
scaled_definition: RaaS the dominant delivery model: Coveware Q4 2020 market led by RaaS brands (Sodinokibi 17.5%, Egregor 12.3%, Ryuk 8.7%); Microsoft describes an industrialised 'cybercrime gig economy'
why_slow_or_fast: SLOW-MEDIUM. The affiliate model took ~4-5 years from first programs (~2015-16) to clear dominance (~2019-20). Needed ecosystem build-out: builders, leak sites, negotiation panels, affiliate recruitment and reputation.
source_title: Ransomware-as-a-service: Understanding the cybercrime gig economy
notes: Availability/first-use dates (~2015-16) are vendor-described, not primary-dated; grade C. Microsoft tracks 35+ families and 250+ actors (2022). DOJ LockBit 2024 confirms the 80/20 affiliate/developer split.

scaled_definition: Majority of ransomware attacks: Coveware Q4 2020 = 70% involved a threat to leak exfiltrated data (up from 50% in Q3 2020), 77% by Q1 2021
why_slow_or_fast: FAST. Maze pioneered public data-leak extortion against Allied Universal in Nov 2019; within ~1 year it was the majority tactic. Low technical barrier (exfiltration already common) and it defeats backups, so it spread quickly.
notes: First public leak: Maze/Allied Universal, BleepingComputer 2019-11-21 ('first time we know of that it has actually happened'). Q3 2020 50% -> Q4 2020 70% -> Q1 2021 77% (Coveware).

technique: Cobalt Strike as criminal C2 standard
scaled_definition: Criminal standard: Proofpoint found threat-actor use +161% 2019->2020 and that criminals were the bulk of attributed Cobalt Strike campaigns in 2020; 'tens of thousands' of organisations targeted
why_slow_or_fast: SLOW. Released 2012 (standalone 3.0 in 2015); first seen with threat actors 2016; became a criminal mainstay ~2020. Legitimate tool repurposed; cracked copies and leaks lowered the barrier over time.
source_title: Cobalt Strike: Favorite Tool from APT to Crimeware
notes: first-use (2016) -> standard (2020) ~4 years; from release (2012) 8 years.

enabling_tech: Browser/plugin exploit packs sold or rented
scaled_definition: Blackhole the dominant malware-delivery method 2012-2013 (Malwarebytes); >1,000 customers at $500-700/month; then DECLINED sharply after the author's Oct 2013 arrest and collapsed by ~2016 (Angler gone Jun 2016)
why_slow_or_fast: MEDIUM up, then COLLAPSE. MPack/WebAttacker (2006) were the first kits; Blackhole (2010) dominated by 2012. A counter-example to permanence: exploit kits scaled then withered as browsers hardened, Flash died, and authors were arrested; attackers reverted to macros and social engineering.
publisher: Wikipedia (citing Trend Micro, RAND, BBC, Malwarebytes)
notes: Blackhole $500-700/mo + $50/mo crypter, >1,000 customers, Paunch arrested Oct 2013 (Krebs 2013-12-06, grade B). Shows scaled use is not permanent. Decline drivers: browser hardening, Flash deprecation, arrests.

enabling_tech: Leaked NSA SMBv1 exploit (Shadow Brokers dump)
scaled_definition: WannaCry hit 200,000+ computers across 150+ countries within days; NotPetya followed in June 2017
why_slow_or_fast: VERY FAST (days). The exploit leaked 14 Apr 2017; Adylkuzz cryptomining began ~24 Apr; WannaCry worm hit on 12 May. A ready-made, reliable, wormable RCE needs no ecosystem, so weaponisation was near-immediate (patch MS17-010 had shipped 14 Mar, a month before the leak).
source_title: Adylkuzz Cryptocurrency Mining Malware Spreading via EternalBlue/DoublePulsar
notes: Leak date 2017-04-14; MS17-010 patch 2017-03-14 (Microsoft bulletin). WannaCry scale from Kaspersky 2017-05-13 (45,000+ day one, 74 countries) and DOJ 2018-09-06 (150+ countries).

scaled_definition: Mass internet-wide exploitation within days: Cloudflare peak 27,439 blocked exploit requests/minute on 12 Dec; coin miners, botnets (Mirai), Cobalt Strike, then ransomware (Khonsari, NightSky by 4 Jan 2022)
why_slow_or_fast: VERY FAST (hours). Public disclosure 9 Dec 2021 (exploitation seen from 1 Dec, before disclosure); mass scanning/cryptomining within hours, ransomware within ~3 weeks. Ubiquitous library + trivial exploit string = immediate, universal weaponisation.
source_title: Exploitation of CVE-2021-44228 before public disclosure
notes: Earliest exploitation 2021-12-01 03:58:34; disclosure tweet 2021-12-09 14:25 UTC; peak 27,439/min 12 Dec. Ransomware (NightSky) by 2021-12/2022-01-04 (Microsoft 2021-12-11).

enabling_tech: Mass of insecure default-credential IoT devices
scaled_definition: Record DDoS within weeks: 620 Gbps on Krebs (20 Sep 2016), ~1 Tbps on OVH, Dyn outage (21 Oct 2016); source-code release (~30 Sep 2016) spawned many variants
why_slow_or_fast: FAST (months). BASHLITE/Gafgyt showed the IoT-botnet model from ~2014; Mirai appeared Aug 2016 and set DDoS records within ~2 months, then the public source release industrialised it. Abundant un-patchable targets and a simple technique.
notes: Mirai first found Aug 2016 (MalwareMustDie); Krebs 620 Gbps 2016-09-20; Dyn 2016-10-21; operators pleaded guilty 2017-12-13. Enabling-tech availability (cheap insecure IoT) ~2014.

scaled_definition: Widespread: FinCEN observed rising deepfake-media SARs 'beginning in 2023 and continuing in 2024'; FBI PSA (Dec 2024) warns of AI voice/video fraud; Arup lost HK$200m/US$25.6m to a deepfake video call (reported 2024)
why_slow_or_fast: SLOW (~5 years). A bespoke CEO-voice fraud (~EUR 220,000, UK energy firm) is reported from 2019, but mass criminal use awaited cheap consumer voice-cloning (ElevenLabs etc., ~2023) and only became common in 2024. Real-time quality and delivery were the bottlenecks.
source_title: FinCEN Alert on Fraud Schemes Involving Deepfake Media
notes: 2019 EUR220k case via prior project/Wikipedia (WSJ/Forbes), grade C, not primary-verified this session. FinCEN alert and FBI PSA I-120324-PSA (2024-12-03) are primary for the widespread phase.

technique: Neural machine translation for non-English phishing/BEC
scaled_definition: NOT FOUND as a measurable share; routine use confirmed qualitatively (FBI PSA Dec 2024: criminals use AI translation 'to limit grammatical or spelling errors'; Trend Micro 2024: translation 'opened markets previously closed')
why_slow_or_fast: POORLY MEASURED. GNMT reached production Sep 2016 and removing tell-tale grammar errors is an obvious fraud use, but no source dates first criminal use or gives a scaled share. Likely a slow, silent diffusion with no clean inflection point.
source_title: A Neural Network for Machine Translation, at Production Scale
notes: First criminal use and scaled share both NOT FOUND. Included to show a technique whose adoption lag cannot be measured. DeepL launched Aug 2017.

scaled_definition: ~10% of malicious email contains AI-assisted text (Verizon DBIR 2025 anchor, ~5%->~10% over two years; DBIR 2026 says it 'doubled' again). Not a dominant share; phishing's share of initial access stayed ~flat
why_slow_or_fast: MEDIUM. First criminal LLM product (WormGPT) ~6-7 months after ChatGPT; ~10% of malicious-email text AI-assisted by ~2024 (~2.5-3 years). Assistive text is cheap but English fraud text was already 'good enough', capping the gain.
notes: ChatGPT 2022-11-30. WormGPT public Jun 2023 (Krebs 2023-08-08, Cato). ~5%->10% anchor is DBIR 2025 via prior project. First underground ChatGPT tooling reported Dec 2022 (Check Point OPWNAI) recalled, not verified this session.

enabling_tech: Open/jailbroken LLMs sold as a service
scaled_definition: NEVER SCALED. WormGPT claimed ~200 paying customers then shut down Aug 2023; FraudGPT could not deliver a working product to researchers (a scam); 2024-25 'WormGPT' variants are thin wrappers over Grok/Mixtral with hundreds of users
why_slow_or_fast: SLOW / NON-EVENT. A feared capability that never scaled: unreliable output, rampant vendor fraud, opsec/logging fears, and the fact that jailbroken mainstream models were cheaper and better. A key counter-example to inevitable adoption.
source_title: The Dilemma of AI: Malicious LLMs
notes: WormGPT ~200 customers, EUR500-5,000, GPT-J, shut 2023-08-08 (Krebs). WormGPT 4: $50/mo, $175/yr, $220 lifetime, 571 subscribers (Unit 42). Talos paid for FraudGPT and got non-working creds (2025-06-25).

enabling_tech: Agentic coding + LLM APIs callable at runtime
scaled_definition: NOT SCALED (isolated/experimental). PROMPTSTEAL (APT28/LAMEHUG, Jun 2025) is the first malware observed querying an LLM in live operations; PROMPTFLUX experimental; GTG-5004 sold AI-built ransomware for $400-$1,200 (Aug 2025)
why_slow_or_fast: EARLY. ~2.5-3 years from ChatGPT to the first live LLM-querying malware; still rare and mostly state or novice-seller. Verbose self-narrating AI-written code is itself a detection signal, which limits the payoff.
source_title: Threat Actor Usage of AI Tools (PROMPTFLUX, PROMPTSTEAL)
notes: PROMPTSTEAL first live LLM-querying malware (Jun 2025, APT28, CERT-UA LAMEHUG). GTG-5004 AI-built ransomware $400-1,200 (Anthropic 2025-08-27).

enabling_tech: Agentic coding tools (Claude Code etc.) + LLM orchestration
scaled_definition: NOT YET SCALED. ~13 publicly documented agentic operations/clusters in ~14 months; under ~0.1-5% of ~10,000 posted ransomware victims a year; every case is lab- or vendor-reported with no denominator
why_slow_or_fast: MID-DIFFUSION, reporting lags ~2-3x shorter than the LLM-text wave. First criminal agentic report (GTG-2002) ~6 months after Claude Code's preview; first state case (GTG-1002) ~8.6 months. Human target-selection and monetisation remain the bottleneck (Amdahl ceiling).
source_title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: August 2025 (GTG-2002)
notes: Claude Code research preview 2025-02-24; GA 2025-05-22. GTG-2002 (>=17 orgs) 2025-08-27; GTG-1002 (~30 targets, 80-90% AI) 2025-11-13. Scaled share does not yet exist.

enabling_tech: Agentic LLM running the full intrusion+encryption chain
scaled_definition: NOT SCALED. Sysdig's JADEPUFFER is billed as the first documented agentic ransomware; CSA counted only two documented autonomous post-exploitation cases in 2026 ('two cases are not yet a statistically established trend'); single victim environment, no leak site
why_slow_or_fast: EARLIEST STAGE. Agent ran 600+ payloads end to end (recon->encryption of 1,342 Nacos configs) via a Langflow RCE (CVE-2025-3248); a human still provisioned infrastructure and chose the victim. One observed case to date.
source_title: JADEPUFFER: Agentic ransomware for automated database extortion
notes: Single vendor, behavioural inference (self-narrating payloads), no model named, no ransom figure, no victim count. ENCFORGE follow-up (CSA 2026-07-26) targets ~180 AI/ML file extensions.

scaled_definition: Rapid adoption through 2017-18 (injected into many compromised sites), then COLLAPSED after Coinhive shut down in March 2019 as Monero value and yields fell
why_slow_or_fast: FAST then COLLAPSE. Adopted within months of Coinhive's launch, but economics (low payout, falling Monero price) and the service's shutdown killed it. Another example that scaled use is not permanent.
notes: DATES RECALLED, NOT PRIMARY-VERIFIED THIS SESSION. Included only as a 'fast-then-collapsed' reference-class example; verify Coinhive launch (Sep 2017) and shutdown (Mar 2019) before print.
